video.title: Trading Psychology: How to Beat Overtrading and Impulsive Clicks | Paradigm Shift

key_passages.text: In 48 BC Julius Caesar faced Pompey at the Battle of Phacilis. Pompey had more troops, more resources. Everyone expected Caesar to attack impulsively to force the fight.
Be ultra-specific. For position sizing, I never risk more than 1% of my account per trade. Write these rules down, print them out on the single piece of paper,
A clean setup appears on gold futures. It checks all the boxes. So Alex risks 1% of his account per his rules.
Number two. Ignoring rules under pressure. Stress amplifies FOMO.
